R2's row listing names no email attribute. The rule's reader finds a user only through the email-index GSI and then requires the row's email to equal the address (canonical_profile_reads.py 70-94). log.streams_denominator_rule: filter-log-events over the group for the window from the first request to the last request plus 5 minutes. Read every page (default auto-pagination, counted client side; never --no-paginate). Print the window, the count of distinct logStreamName values in the results, and the total match count. Zero streams searched is VOID. The expected total is three lines, one per request, in request order. A total other than three is not attributed to the identities, because the line carries no identity: other internal selections in the window write the same line. That case is a surprise row, not a guess
log.positive_control: the active arm's admitted line is the positive control. If it is absent, admission was not observed and the exercise is void for the admitted expectation

removal.method: after the later of the three exp values has passed, delete the PROFILE items of disabled and active (DeleteItem on PK USER#<address>, SK PROFILE, condition attribute_exists(PK)). Then read all three addresses by the rule's own path: a GSI query on email-index AND a ConsistentRead GetItem of USER#<address>/PROFILE. ABSENT is required on both reads for all three addresses (norow was ABSENT before the sitting and is read again). The GSI is eventually consistent, so a single ABSENT GSI read is repeated until it holds, within a bounded window that is printed. The token is held only in the executor process and is never written to a file, a log or a trace. A PRESENT read after the delete is a STOP
removal.exp_rule: exp minus iat is at most 1200 seconds; the removal waits for the later exp; no identity outlives the sitting; a second token is not covered
